page: Google Cloud Platform n1-highmem-4 is an x86_64 architecture virtual machine belonging to the n1 server family. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel Xeon cores running at 2.3 GHz, with hyper-threading enabled. The instance is configured with 26.0 GB of system memory, providing a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 6.5 GB per core. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators.

Benchmark evaluations place this instance's performance primarily in the lower tiers. The single-core and multi-core CPU capabilities, measured via stress-ng and Geekbench, fall into the bottom 25% and bottom 10% categories. Memory bandwidth tests show 162.39 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 25.86 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Cryptographic and compression tasks, such as gzip and bzip3, also register in the lower percentiles.

From a resource density perspective, the n1-highmem-4 offers a higher memory allocation relative to its compute capacity compared to standard general-purpose instances. This profile is suitable for memory-intensive workloads that do not demand high CPU throughput, such as caching layers, small database instances, or lightweight enterprise applications. However, the older Intel Xeon architecture and lower benchmark scores suggest a tradeoff in raw processing efficiency compared to newer instance generations.
